DEV-TASK-SUM.title: The sum of an array's elements
DEV-TASK-SUM.description: Write a program that reads n integers from standard input and prints their sum.
DEV-TASK-SUM.instructions: The first line holds n, the second n integers separated by spaces. Print the sum on one line.

DAS-S1-A1.title: A first program: a greeting
DAS-S1-A1.description: Write a program that reads the user's name and greets them.
DAS-S1-A1.instructions: Input: a name on one line (it may contain spaces). Output: Salom, <name>! (the greeting is in Uzbek — that is how the tests check it).
DAS-S1-A1.constraintsText: The name is 1 to 100 characters long.

DAS-S1-A2.title: Arithmetic operations
DAS-S1-A2.description: For two integers, compute the sum, the difference, the product, the integer quotient and the remainder.
DAS-S1-A2.instructions: Input: a and b on one line. Output: on five lines a+b, a-b, a*b, a div b, a mod b.
DAS-S1-A2.constraintsText: 0 ≤ a ≤ 10^9, 1 ≤ b ≤ 10^9. The product may not fit in 32 bits: use long in Java.

DAS-S1-A3.title: A leap year
DAS-S1-A3.description: Decide with logical operations whether a year is a leap year. A year divisible by 4 is a leap year, but one divisible by 100 and not by 400 is not.
DAS-S1-A3.instructions: Input: a year. Output: Kabisa (a leap year) or Kabisa emas (not a leap year) — the answer is in Uzbek, as the tests check it.
hints: A year divisible by 100 is a leap year only if it is also divisible by 400: 1900 is not a leap year, 2000 is.

DAS-S1-A4.title: The number of roots of a quadratic equation
DAS-S1-A4.description: Use a conditional statement to decide how many real roots the equation ax² + bx + c = 0 has.
DAS-S1-A4.instructions: Input: the integers a b c (a ≠ 0). Output: 0, 1 or 2.
DAS-S1-A4.constraintsText: |a|, |b|, |c| ≤ 10^6. Compute the discriminant as a long.

DAS-S1-A5.title: The day of the week (the selection statement)
DAS-S1-A5.description: Print the name of the day of the week for a number from 1 to 7. Use the match statement in Python and switch in Java.
DAS-S1-A5.instructions: Input: an integer n. Output: the day's name in Uzbek (Dushanba, Seshanba, Chorshanba, Payshanba, Juma, Shanba, Yakshanba), or Xato for a wrong number — that is how the tests check the answer.

DAS-S1-A6.title: The factorial (a counted loop)
DAS-S1-A6.constraintsText: 0 ≤ n ≤ 20 (the result fits in a long).
hints: 0! = 1. Start the variable that holds the result at 1.
The loop goes from 2 to n and multiplies the result by i at each step. 20! does not fit in a plain int — a 64-bit type is needed.

DAS-S1-A7.title: Testing for a prime
DAS-S1-A7.description: Check with a while loop whether a number is prime: look for a divisor from 2 up to √n.
DAS-S1-A7.instructions: Input: n. Output: Tub (prime) or Tub emas (not prime) — the answer is in Uzbek, as the tests check it.
hints: 1 is not a prime number. Check this case separately.
It is enough to look for a divisor not up to n but only while d * d <= n.
Stop the loop as soon as the first divisor is found — there is no need to check the rest.

DAS-S1-A8.title: A multiplication table (a nested loop)
DAS-S1-A8.description: Print the n × n multiplication table with nested loops.
DAS-S1-A8.instructions: Input: n. Output: n lines; line i holds the numbers i·1, i·2, …, i·n separated by one space.

DAS-S1-A9B.title: Linear search in an array
DAS-S1-A9B.description: Find the position (from 1) where the value x first appears in an array. If it is not there, print -1.
DAS-S1-A9B.instructions: Input: n; n integers; x. Output: the position or -1.

DAS-S1-MT1.title: A piecewise function
DAS-S1-MT1.description: Compute the function y = x² (for x < 0), y = 2x + 1 (for 0 ≤ x ≤ 10), y = x − 10 (for x > 10).
DAS-S1-MT1.instructions: Input: an integer x. Output: y.

DAS-S1-MT2.title: The sum of the harmonic series
DAS-S1-MT2.description: Compute the sum S = 1 + 1/2 + 1/3 + … + 1/n and print it with 4 decimal places.
DAS-S1-MT2.instructions: Input: n. Output: S, 4 digits after the point.
DAS-S1-MT2.constraintsText: 1 ≤ n ≤ 10^6. In Java use String.format(Locale.US, "%.4f", s).

DAS-S1-MT3.title: Printing an array in reverse order
DAS-S1-MT3.description: Print the elements of an array in reverse order.
DAS-S1-MT3.instructions: Input: n; n integers. Output: the elements in reverse order, separated by spaces.

DAS-S1-MT4.title: The diagonals of a matrix
DAS-S1-MT4.description: Find the sums of the elements on the main and secondary diagonals of an n × n matrix.
DAS-S1-MT4.instructions: Input: n; then n lines of n integers. Output: two numbers on one line — the sum of the main diagonal and the sum of the secondary diagonal.

DAS-S1-MT5.title: The dot product of vectors
DAS-S1-MT5.description: Compute the dot product of two n-dimensional vectors: a₁b₁ + a₂b₂ + … + aₙbₙ.
DAS-S1-MT5.instructions: Input: n; the vector a (n numbers); the vector b (n numbers). Output: the dot product.

DAS-S1-MT6.title: Pairs with sum k
DAS-S1-MT6.description: Use nested loops to find the number of pairs with i < j and aᵢ + aⱼ = k.
DAS-S1-MT6.instructions: Input: n and k; n integers. Output: the number of pairs.

DAS-Q-M2.title: Programming basics: a review quiz
DAS-Q-M2.description: A short quiz on the first two lectures: algorithms, variables, data types and operations.
DAS-Q-M2.instructions: The quiz has 7 questions of different kinds: choosing an option, entering a number or a word, ordering and matching. Read every question carefully.

questions.explanation: An algorithm is a precise, finite sequence of steps that leads to the solution of a problem. It does not depend on any programming language.

options.text: A precise sequence of steps for solving a problem
The computing device of a computer
The file in which a program's code is kept

questions.prompt: Which of these values belong to the integer type (int)?
questions.explanation: 42 and −7 are integers. 3.14 is a floating-point number (float), and "25" in quotes is a string (str).

questions.prompt: A variable name may start with a digit.
questions.explanation: In Python, Java and C++ a variable name starts with a letter or an underscore; a digit may only come later.

questions.prompt: What is the value of the expression 17 % 5? (% is the remainder of division)
Write the name of the Python function that prints text on the screen.
questions.explanation: The print() function prints the values given to it on the screen.

questions.prompt: Put the stages of creating a program in the right order.
questions.explanation: First the problem is analysed, then the algorithm is designed, the code is written, and finally the program is tested.

questions.prompt: Match each value with its data type.
questions.explanation: 42 is an integer, 3.14 a floating-point number, "salom" a string, True a boolean value.
